svg.title: How a call flows
svg.desc: One pickup call as a transcript, in three columns: what is said on the phone, the stations the sentence passes, and what the code does with it. The caller's words pass the access, Asterisk, the ear and the conversation core; the agent's reply goes from the core through the mouth, Asterisk and the access. The core is the only station that reaches the code; where it asks the LLM, the LLM hangs above the core, linked to it alone. The caller orders: get_service_status and search_menu, one tool per hop, at most six, each run by the core against Postgres; the LLM has no line to a tool or the database. With the caller's name the core runs draft_order, every price from Postgres. The LLM reads the draft back word for word, and the core checks that the caller heard it. Only after the caller's yes does the core run confirm. The core says the booking itself from confirm's result, not the model; meanwhile the tablet shows the order. The slip waits for the team's approval, in primary mode up to the amount limit it is due at once, as in this call. Set apart, the ways to the team: the core checks for a complaint before the model; for a complaint no rule covers, when the AI is unsure or the model fails, the team phone rings while the restaurant is open; after hours, when the caller's number is known, a callback waits on the tablet. When the service voice fails, the exchange rings the team phone. Each station's edge shows whether it is built, in progress or planned.
